Beef frank, poppy seed bun, the full garden.How to make it8 all-beef frankfurts8 poppy seed split-top rolls4 tbsp yellow mustard4 tbsp bright green sweet relish1 white onion, finely diced2 tomatoes, cut in thin wedges8 dill pickle spears8 pickled sport peppers or small hot pickled chillies1 tsp celery saltBring a pot of water to a bare simmer, add the franks and heat through without boiling.Steam or warm the rolls so they stay soft.Tuck a frank into each roll and dress in order: mustard, relish, onion, tomato wedges, a pickle spear and two peppers.Finish with a pinch of celery salt. No tomato sauce.Provasic-free chicken liver pate with toastKimble finds Provasic damages the liver. Silky livers, butter, thyme, toasted rye.How to make it400g chicken livers, trimmed150g butter, softened2 French shallots, finely diced1 garlic clove, crushed4 thyme sprigs, leaves picked60ml brandy8 slices of rye bread, toasted8 cornichonsMelt 30g of the butter and soften the shallot, garlic and thyme.Turn up the heat, add the livers and cook until browned outside and just pink inside.Add the brandy and let it bubble off, then cool for 5 minutes.Blend with the rest of the butter and plenty of salt and pepper until silky, press into a dish and chill.Serve with the rye toast and cornichons.Hospital cafeteria jelly cupsLime, for St Patrick's week.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.Main MealCook County Italian beef, dipped, with hot giardinieraKimble poses as a Cook County janitor. Thin roast beef, garlicky jus, pickled chilli veg.How to make it1.2kg beef blade or topside roast6 garlic cloves, crushed2 tsp dried oregano1 tsp chilli flakes1 tsp fennel seeds1 L beef stock4 long crusty Italian rolls1 red capsicum, finely diced1 celery stick, finely diced1 carrot, finely diced2 long green chillies, sliced125ml white vinegar125ml olive oilFor the giardiniera, toss the capsicum, celery, carrot and chillies with a tablespoon of salt, leave 15 minutes, rinse, then cover with the vinegar and oil.Rub the beef with the garlic, oregano, chilli and fennel, sit it in a roasting dish and pour the stock around it.Roast covered at 160°C until just tender, then rest and chill if you can, so it slices thinly.Slice the beef as thin as possible and warm it in the hot pan juices.Pile into the split rolls, dip the whole sandwich in the jus and top with giardiniera.St Patrick's Day corned beef with buttered cabbageGerard loses him in the parade. Corned silverside, cabbage, spuds, mustard sauce.How to make it1.5kg corned silverside1 brown onion, halved2 bay leaves1 tbsp brown sugar1 tbsp malt vinegar600g small potatoes1/2 green cabbage, cut in wedges40g butter150ml thickened cream2 tbsp wholegrain mustardRinse the silverside, cover with cold water and add the onion, bay, sugar and vinegar.Simmer very gently until a skewer slides in easily.Lift the beef out to rest and cook the potatoes in the liquid, adding the cabbage for the last few minutes.Drain, toss the cabbage and potatoes with the butter, warm the cream with the mustard and serve with thick slices of beef.DessertThink-me-up chocolate donuts with sprinklesGerard wants a donut with little sprinkles. Yeast donuts, chocolate glaze, rainbow sprinkles.How to make it375g plain flour7g sachet dried yeast50g caster sugar185ml warm milk1 egg50g butter, melted1 L vegetable oil, for frying150g dark chocolate, chopped80ml thickened cream3 tbsp rainbow sprinklesMix the flour, yeast, sugar and a pinch of salt, then add the milk, egg and butter and knead until smooth and springy.Cover and leave somewhere warm until doubled.Roll out 1.5cm thick, cut 8 rings and prove for 30 minutes more.Fry at 175°C for a minute a side until golden, then drain.Melt the chocolate into the warm cream, dip the tops of the donuts and shower with sprinkles.DrinksBig Dog pale ale from Goose IslandNever argue with the Big Dog.
